title: Turn the viewer's file references and command rows into direct, translated controls

needs: Wherever the viewer shows a file it calls it `path` and prints the path itself -- a single copy-to-clipboard button carrying the whole string (report Input, report Output/Artefact, render provenance). The operator's actual intent is almost never 'I want this string': it is 'open this file', 'show me where it sits', and only sometimes 'give me the text'. One control serves the rarest of the three.

The render panel offers `blender <path>` as a command to copy and paste into a terminal. Opening a .blend file is what the host system's file association already does; asking the operator to open a terminal to do it is a longer route to the same place.

`List operations` and `Check setup` run for real on a served page (adr_007) but their result is dumped as raw process stdout into a `<pre>` inside the still-open menu dropdown: untranslated, unstyled, and shown in a container sized for a menu row. `Check setup` in particular prints a JSON object at the operator.

Both rows sit in menus that do not describe them: `List operations` under File and `Check setup` under File, while both are reference material about the tool and its environment rather than actions on the current project.
context: adr_007 closed the set of commands a served page may run to three fixed argument lists and stated the rule that makes it safe: `no operator-supplied value ever reaches the subprocess`. Opening or revealing a file is by nature parameterised by a file, so it cannot join that set as-is. The shape that preserves the rule is an allow-list the *server* owns: the build already knows every file the page can name (report inputs, outputs, renders), so the page can send an identifier into that set and never a path -- surfaced here as the decision to record, not pre-decided.

A `file://` page has no server to reach. Under adr_007 that is not a degraded case to work around but the baseline: the Open and Reveal controls have nothing to call there and must be absent or visibly unavailable, with Copy path still working exactly as it does today.

`meshanvil doctor` already emits a machine-readable object and the viewer already reads a cached copy of it from `work/doctor.json` for the start screen; `meshanvil list` prints formatted text only. A modal that translates a result should read structured data, not scrape a subprocess's stdout -- which likely means `list` gains a machine-readable form rather than the page learning to parse its columns.

Icon-only controls are an accessibility surface, not just a smaller button: each needs an accessible name from the catalogue (adr on i18n applies -- no inline English), and the icon set has to stay dependency-free like the rest of the viewer, so inline SVG or text glyphs, not an icon font.

This request should land after `req_010_make_the_viewer_refresh_itself_and_give_the_code_a_module_structure_that_holds`, which splits `viewer/viewer.js` into modules and introduces a built client bundle. Implementing this one first would rewrite the same code twice.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Every place the viewer labels a file reference calls it `file`, not `path`, in both catalogues, and no label reads `path` where a file is meant.

AC2: Every file reference the viewer shows (report Input, report Output/Artefact, render provenance, and any other) offers the same three controls -- Open, Copy path, Reveal -- rendered as icons with no visible text label, each carrying an accessible name resolved from the string catalogue.

AC3: On a served page, Open launches the file through the host system's default handler and Reveal opens the containing folder with the file selected where the platform supports it; both are verified on the platform under test and the platforms not verified are stated as unverified.

AC4: On a `file://` page, Copy path behaves exactly as it does today and Open and Reveal are not offered as controls that appear to work -- absent or explicitly shown as unavailable, never silently inert.

AC5: A decision is recorded (an amendment to adr_007 or a new ADR) covering how a file reaches the server without an operator-supplied path becoming a subprocess argument, and the implementation matches it.
AC6: No `blender <path>` command is offered for copying anywhere in the viewer; opening a report's artefact goes through the Open control of AC2.

AC7: `List operations` and `Check setup`, run from a served page, present their result in a modal built from structured data, with every operator-facing string resolved from the catalogue and available in both languages -- no raw process stdout and no JSON shown to the operator.
AC8: Opening either modal closes the menu it was launched from, and the modal is dismissible by the same means as the start screen modal.
AC9: `List operations` and `Check setup` are both reached from the Help menu and appear in no other menu.

AC11: The Help menu's `Create a runbook <report-id>` row -- left copy-only by `adr_007` because its id is a placeholder with no report behind it -- either carries a real report id or states in the row why it does not; no row shows a placeholder that reads as a value.

AC10: `scripts/viewer_smoke.py` covers the new controls and modals so the behaviour cannot silently regress: the three-control group's presence and accessible names, the `file://` degradation, and both modals rendering translated content rather than raw output.

product.title: Direct controls over the files and results the viewer already names
product.overview: Takes the viewer past showing a file reference or a command result as text: a file becomes something to open or locate, and a command result becomes a translated panel, without the viewer gaining a dependency or an open execution surface.
goals: A file reference is a place the operator can go, not a string to copy and retype.
Nothing routes the operator through a terminal for something the host system already does.
A command's result is presented in the operator's language, in a container built for it.
Menu rows sit in the menu that describes them.
non_goals: Opening arbitrary operator-typed paths; whatever is added stays closed and derived from what the build already knows, per adr_007.
A general file browser inside the viewer.
An icon library or any new runtime dependency.

backlog_items.title: Replace each file reference with an icon-only open, copy and reveal group
problem: A file reference is shown as its own path text under the label `path`, wrapped in one copy-to-clipboard button, so the two things an operator usually wants -- open it, show me where it is -- have no control at all.
The render panel routes opening a .blend file through a `blender <path>` command the operator must paste into a terminal.
scope_in: One shared renderer for a file reference, used everywhere the viewer prints one, producing three icon-only controls with catalogue-resolved accessible names.
Renaming the `path` label to `file` in both catalogues.
Removing the `blender <path>` copy command in favour of the Open control.
The `file://` presentation: Copy path unchanged, Open and Reveal not offered as working controls.
scope_out: The server side of Open and Reveal -- the item below owns that.
Any icon library or new dependency; inline SVG or text glyphs only.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: One renderer produces the three-control group and every file reference in the viewer uses it.
AC2: Each control has an accessible name from the catalogue and no visible text label.
AC3: No catalogue string labels a file reference `path`.
AC4: No `blender <path>` command is offered anywhere.
AC5: On a `file://` page Copy path works and the other two are not presented as working controls.

backlog_items.title: Let the served page open and reveal a file the build already knows
problem: Opening a file and revealing its folder are host-system actions the page cannot perform itself, and adr_007's closed command set takes no operator-supplied value, so neither fits the existing `/run` endpoint.
scope_in: A recorded decision (adr_007 amendment or a new ADR) on how a file is named to the server without a page-supplied path reaching a subprocess.
The server side: resolving a reference the build owns to a real file, opening it through the host default handler, and revealing its containing folder, per platform.
Refusal behaviour for a reference the build does not own, and for a file that no longer exists.
scope_out: Opening anything the current build did not already name.
Any change to the three existing `/run` commands.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: An ADR records the rule and the implementation matches it.
AC2: Open launches a report's artefact through the host default handler on the platform under test.
AC3: Reveal opens the containing folder, with the file selected where the platform supports it.
AC4: A reference the build does not own is refused, and a missing file is refused with a distinguishable result rather than silently doing nothing.
AC5: Platforms not verified are recorded as unverified.

backlog_items.title: Show list and setup results as translated modals reached from Help
problem: `List operations` and `Check setup` dump raw, untranslated process stdout -- a JSON object in the case of setup -- into a `<pre>` inside the menu dropdown that launched them, which stays open behind it.
Both rows sit in the File menu though neither acts on the current project.
scope_in: A machine-readable form of the operations list, so the modal renders structured data rather than parsing formatted output.
A modal for each result, built from the catalogue in both languages, dismissible like the start screen modal.
Closing the launching menu when a modal opens.
Moving both rows into the Help menu.

The Help menu's `Create a runbook <report-id>` row, which `adr_007` left copy-only because its id is a placeholder with no report behind it: either give it the selected report as a real target, or state in the row why it stays a command to copy.
scope_out: Changing what either command does or what it reports.
`Preview pruning`, which keeps its current presentation in this slice.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The operations list is available in a machine-readable form and the modal renders from it.
AC2: Both modals show catalogue-resolved strings in both languages, with no raw stdout and no JSON visible to the operator.
AC3: Opening either modal leaves no menu open behind it, and it is dismissible like the start screen modal.
AC4: Both rows are in Help and in no other menu.
AC5: The `Create a runbook` row either carries a real report id or says why it does not; no row shows a placeholder that looks like a value.

backlog_items.title: Cover the new controls and modals in the viewer smoke suite
problem: The three-control group, the `file://` degradation and the two modals are all presentation behaviour that no existing check would notice regressing.
scope_in: Assertions in `scripts/viewer_smoke.py` for the control group's presence and accessible names, the `file://` degradation, and both modals rendering translated content.
scope_out: A new test framework or runner; the existing smoke suite is where this lives.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The smoke suite fails if a file reference loses any of its three controls or its accessible names.
AC2: The smoke suite fails if a `file://` page presents Open or Reveal as working controls.
AC3: The smoke suite fails if either modal shows raw output instead of translated content.

orchestration_task.title: Deliver the viewer's direct file controls and translated result modals
plan: 1. Record the decision on how a file reaches the server without an operator-supplied path, amending adr_007 or adding an ADR.
2. Build the server side of Open and Reveal against a build-owned reference set, with its refusals.
3. Replace every file reference with the shared icon-only open/copy/reveal group, rename the label to file, and drop the blender command.
4. Give the operations list a machine-readable form and render both results as translated modals reached from Help.
5. Extend the viewer smoke suite over the new controls, the file:// degradation and both modals.
6. Re-run make check, viewer-smoke and the Logics gates before closeout.
